headline: Acquisitions boost revenue, financing costs squeeze profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 45.1% y/y to $1,985 million (4.2% organic) on the Coltel deal and Ecuador/Uruguay consolidation, but net profit attributable to owners fell 43.4% to $109 million ($0.65 diluted EPS) as financing costs, integration severance, and minority-interest losses offset the topline gain.
summary_long: Millicom's Q1 2026 revenue jumped 45.1% (4.2% organic) to $1,985M on the Coltel acquisition and Ecuador/Uruguay consolidation; Adjusted EBITDA rose 35.5% to $857M. Operating profit slipped 1.2% to $416M on $65M Colombia integration severance and higher D&A from the larger perimeter. Net financial expenses rose $77M on acquisition debt, and ~$67M of restructuring charges plus a swing to minority-interest losses drove net profit attributable to owners down 43.4% to $109M ($0.65 diluted EPS, from $1.14). Equity free cash flow improved to $225M (+66.5% ex last year's infrastructure sale). Net debt rose $2,253M q/q to $7,609M on acquisition payments, lifting leverage to 2.76x from 2.17x. Management targets FY2026 EFCF of at least $900M and year-end leverage around 2.5x.

drivers.explanation: Coltel consolidation plus the Ecuador/Uruguay additions drove headline revenue and EBITDA growth, but net profit fell as acquisition financing costs, integration severance, and minority-interest losses outweighed the operating gains.
Growth of 45.1% was driven by the Coltel acquisition, the Ecuador/Uruguay consolidation, FX tailwinds in Colombia/Paraguay/Bolivia, and continued Mobile and B2B revenue growth.
EBITDA rose 35.5% on $33 million from the Coltel consolidation, savings from the efficiency program, and the impact of M&A and restructuring-related one-offs reflected in 2026 results.

Operating profit fell 1.2% as $65 million of Colombia integration severance and higher D&A from the expanded perimeter offset revenue growth; other operating income also declined on Colombia network-asset transfers.

Net profit fell 43.4% on $77 million higher net financial expenses tied to acquisition debt, roughly $67 million of restructuring charges on newly acquired operations, and a swing to minority-interest losses from Coltel.
EPS fell to $0.65 from $1.14, tracking the net profit decline, on a slightly smaller weighted-average share count of 167.25 million versus 169.2 million a year earlier.

EFCF rose to $225 million from $177 million (+66.5% excluding last year's infrastructure sale) on $221 million higher Adjusted EBITDA and improved working capital, partly offset by higher cash capex and spectrum payments.

Net debt rose $2,253 million q/q to $7,609 million, driven by $773 million of acquisition payments (Tigo UNE, Coltel, Telefónica Chile) and Coltel's consolidated debt, partly offset by EFCF generation.
Leverage climbed to 2.76x from 2.17x as acquisition-related debt in Colombia and Chile outpaced EBITDA growth; management targets year-end 2026 leverage of around 2.5x.
